label: Bible Study
prompt: The beauty of Israel is slain upon thy high places: how are the _____ fallen!
verse: The beauty of Israel is slain upon thy high places: how are the mighty fallen!
note: David's lament for Saul and Jonathan — 'how are the mighty fallen' repeats three times in the song.

label: Warm-Up Word
prompt: And when they were come up out of the water, the Spirit of the Lord caught away Philip, that the eunuch saw him no more: and he went on his way _____.
verse: And when they were come up out of the water, the Spirit of the Lord caught away Philip, that the eunuch saw him no more: and he went on his way rejoicing.
note: Freshly baptized on a desert road, the Ethiopian treasurer went on his way rejoicing.

label: Sunday School
prompt: And a certain man drew a bow at a _____, and smote the king of Israel between the joints of the harness: wherefore he said unto the driver of his chariot, Turn thine hand, and carry me out of the host; for I am wounded.
verse: And a certain man drew a bow at a venture, and smote the king of Israel between the joints of the harness: wherefore he said unto the driver of his chariot, Turn thine hand, and carry me out of the host; for I am wounded.
note: A soldier drew his bow 'at a venture' — at random — and the disguised king of Israel couldn't hide from it.

label: Deep Water
prompt: Whereby are given unto us exceeding great and precious promises: that by these ye might be _____ of the divine nature, having escaped the corruption that is in the world through lust.
verse: Whereby are given unto us exceeding great and precious promises: that by these ye might be partakers of the divine nature, having escaped the corruption that is in the world through lust.
note: One of Scripture's boldest lines: through God's promises, believers come to share the divine nature itself.

label: Don't Play With Me
prompt: And while he _____, the men laid hold upon his hand, and upon the hand of his wife, and upon the hand of his two daughters; the LORD being merciful unto him: and they brought him forth, and set him without the city.
verse: And while he lingered, the men laid hold upon his hand, and upon the hand of his wife, and upon the hand of his two daughters; the LORD being merciful unto him: and they brought him forth, and set him without the city.
note: Even with judgment at the door, Lot 'lingered' — so the angels took him by the hand, 'the LORD being merciful unto him.'
